title: Working on my first game with no game dev background - a cozy little incremental terraforming game: Wakeling
author: jchr85
selftext:
Hello all,

  
As many here, I've always been interested in making my ideas come to life and be able to create something that may bring joy. I have absolutely zero background within game dev though (having a background as an ERP implementation consultant instead), so it's always stayed as a happy dream for "maybe in the future sometime".

  
But now that AI has become so competent I've finally given it a shot and have been experimenting some, and am currently working on a cozy little incremental game where you're gradually bringing back life to a planet as a cute little alien, which I'm starting to feel quite happy with how it's coming along. Some of the art/models needs more work and are not final assets yet, especially your hearth/main building. 

The premise of the game is:

  
You’re a little larva that crash-lands on a dead planet. You eat the dead crust, and living weave grows in your trail. Roots spread from your Hearth, little creatures start working for you, and you mutate your body and grow new organs. Phase by phase you raise the air, heat and water, melt the ice into lakes, and the weave turns to moss, mushroom forest and finally jungle – until you wake the planet’s heart.

**How I’m making it without knowing how to make games**

* **Code:** Godot 4 with C#, written together with Claude Code. I describe what I want, play it and say what feels off, and it writes and tests the code. 
* **Art:** concept art and the logo made with image generation (Chat GPT), then turned into 3D models with Tripo/Hunyuan 3D. Blender scripts clean up each model and split it into parts that can animate (wings, legs, heads).
* **Balancing:** since I can’t playtest 3 hours after every change, a bot plays the whole game in about 15 minutes and writes a report on where the player waits and which resource runs short. Most of the pacing came from comparing those runs.
* **Not AI:** the music is [Cozy Tunes by Pizza Doggy](https://pizzadoggy.itch.io/cozy-tunes), and the fonts are Fredoka and Nunito.



**Biggest obstacles I've faced (so far)**

* Having no background and this being my first try at making a game, everything, heh.
* I didn't have a clear picture on exactly how I wanted the end result to be, so that has slowed down progress. When I started I was first aiming for something more in line with the Zerg and creep from Starcraft and a darker tone, but I found I enjoyed this tone better for this kind of game. 
* I had a GDD written, but looking back I probably should have had it more fleshed out before starting the actual work.
* Art and models. I have absolutely no knowledge in this or how to create assets myself so I've relied on image gen and creating models out of it with AI 3D modeling tools. It gives... varied.. results. Blender has worked decently to finetune and split the models, but not for everything. Especially the main building, which is hollow. AI 3D modeling tools have not produced a good result for me, and trying to fix them in blender gives me all kind issues with missing textures, "blocky" cutouts etc, and trying to recreate the model in Blender does not generate a better result for me (yet, at least).

  
It’s the first time I’ve shown it to anyone outside my own head, so any feedback is very welcome. 

There's no playable demo yet, so probably most on the art and art direction at this point, and if it looks interesting and something you'd be interested in playing :)

comments.author: keytonw
comments.body: Nice work! I’ve always wondered if a terraforming game could work. I’ve seen lots of attempts. But a cozy take is new. Hopefully you’re able to capture some of that pressure washing vibe but with a bit more substance. Love it!

replies.author: jchr85
replies.body:
Thank you! :)

Yeah, that's kind of the vibe I'm trying to capture. The satisfaction of seeing something gradually change over time :)
